S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.

subtypes.Skin Defects: Excessive preoccupation with practically invisible acne, scars, or complexion.
subtypes.Facial Features: Preoccupation with the shape or size of the nose, eyes, or mouth, which appear normal to others.
subtypes.Asymmetry: Excessive obsession with the face or body not being perfectly symmetrical.
subtypes.Muscle Dysmorphia: The belief that one's body is too small or insufficiently muscular despite being normal or muscular.
subtypes.Specific Body Parts: Obsession that specific parts like hair, teeth, or chest are ugly or abnormal.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.

subtypes.Mirror Checking or Avoidance: Compulsively checking oneself in the mirror frequently or, conversely, avoiding mirrors strictly.
subtypes.Excessive Camouflaging: Spending excessive time and effort to hide perceived flaws using makeup, clothes, hats, or sunglasses.
subtypes.Skin Picking: Picking or manipulating the skin excessively to remove or 'fix' flaws.
subtypes.Reassurance Seeking: Repetitively asking others for confirmation that one's appearance is okay or not strange.
subtypes.Comparing: Constantly comparing one's body parts with those of passersby or celebrities.
subtypes.Seeking Cosmetic Procedures: Repeatedly seeking or receiving plastic surgery or dermatological procedures.

symptom.disease_info: Body Dysmorphic Disorder (BDD) is characterized by a persistent, distressing preoccupation with perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear minor to others. Individuals often engage in repetitive behaviors (e.g., mirror checking, comparing, grooming, camouflaging) or mental acts in response to these concerns, which consume significant time and cause functional impairment. The onset is typically in adolescence and the course tends to be chronic, with exacerbations linked to social evaluation, appearance-focused contexts, or stress; insight can range from good to delusional. BDD is distinguished from normal appearance concerns and from eating disorders by the intensity of the preoccupation, the degree of impairment, and the focus on specific perceived defects rather than primarily on weight or body shape.

patient.stressor: Leyda’s concerns about her appearance became more pronounced in the years surrounding perimenopause, as subtle age-related changes coincided with her children becoming more independent and her taking on a more public-facing role at the law office. Being introduced as the experienced paralegal at community workshops for immigrant families meant standing under bright lights, appearing in firm newsletters, and occasionally being in group photos, all of which heightened her focus on perceived flaws she felt were "showing more with age." She gradually started declining speaking opportunities, rearranging her schedule to avoid video calls, and spending increasing time getting ready for work, which her husband and coworkers noticed as a shift from her previously practical, low-fuss routines. She agreed to see a clinician after missing a book club meeting and a community-center workshop she had organized because she felt she "couldn’t let anyone see" her that day, and her primary care physician, noting the impact on her functioning despite normal physical exams, recommended a psychiatric evaluation.
patient.chief_complaint: Lately I can’t stop dwelling on how my face and body look as I’m aging, and it’s making me avoid things I used to do without thinking.

S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.
S067.manifestation: It feels like all I can see when I look in the mirror now are these sagging lines around my mouth and my neck starting to droop, like my whole face is collapsing, and I keep thinking everyone at work must be noticing how old and worn-out I look even if they say they don't see it.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.
S068.manifestation: Most mornings I lose almost an hour standing under the bathroom light putting on and wiping off makeup, tilting my head different ways, zooming in on my face with my phone camera, changing outfits to hide my neck and arms, and asking my husband if I look 'too old' before I finally force myself out the door or sometimes just cancel plans altogether.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve started turning down presentations at the firm, canceling social plans at the last minute, and even showing up late to work because I’m so focused on how I look that I can’t get out the door on time, and my supervisor has hinted that it’s affecting how reliable I seem.
